messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — Elevated 5xx rate detected for /v1/generate in us-west-2. Impacting ~18% of requests. Paging on-call.

maria (oncall): on it. ACKing pager. looking at metrics and recent deploys.

jen (sre): seeing spike at 10:47 UTC. error class = kv-cache:timeout and model-worker OOMs on some hosts. rolling restart of pool-1 in progress.

maria (oncall): if restarts don't stabilize, plan B is route traffic to fallback model variant (fastgen-0.9) and scale up the smaller pool. initiating now.

kai (platform): started autoscale for fallback pool, +8 instances queued. will also enable prefix cache bypass on new instances to reduce KV pressure.

ops (eng-ops): drafting status page copy — initial notice and customer impact. dropping draft below for review. pls +1 or edit.

ops (eng-ops): ```Initial notice (draft): We are investigating an elevated error rate impacting text generation (US-West). Some requests may return 5xx or experience increased latency. Engineers are actively mitigating; a temporary fallback model may be used to reduce error rates while we stabilize. Next update in 30 minutes.```

anna (marketing): edit suggestion — call out affected API path (/v1/generate) and add guidance for customers to retry with exponential backoff; avoid promising ETA. also ask support to flag high-severity tickets.

joe (legal): non-blocking: keep language factual and avoid implying SLA breach until root cause confirmed. pls keep ‘investigating’ / ‘mitigating’ phrasing.

jen (sre): update — rolling restarts completed on 6/8 hosts; error rate fell to ~6% but tail latency still elevated. fallback routing in place for 20% of traffic. monitoring.

maria (oncall): going to publish initial status page now with ops copy + anna edits and joe wording. Support notified to triage incoming tickets as P1 if customer-impacting.

ops (eng-ops): publish command (internal): `deploy-statuspage --component=generation-api --state=investigating --message-file=incidents/1765432199/msg1.md` — done. status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1765432199 :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Status page update published by maria (oncall) at 10:58 UTC.

anna (marketing): pushing a short customer email copy to support: "We’re investigating an intermittent issue affecting text generation in US-West. You may see errors or higher latency for /v1/generate. Our engineers are mitigating and we will update soon."

maria (oncall): next update scheduled in 30m or earlier if we reach <1% errors. tagging incident as active.

jen (sre): note for postmortem — investigate KV cache eviction/growth and worker memory regression from last model rollout. capturing logs and heap dumps.

kai (platform): adding an automatic fallback policy to routing so compatible clients will move to fastgen-0.9 when errors >5% for >2min. helps reduce blast radius.

ops (eng-ops): follow-up draft for 30m update (for review): ```Update: error rate reduced to ~4–6% after targeted restarts and fallback routing. Some customers may still see failures; we continue to scale capacity and investigate root cause. No data loss. Next update in 1 hour or when resolved.```

joe (legal): looks fine. keep the "No data loss" claim if you're confident.

maria (oncall): publishing 30m update now. support, please apply temporary internal tag "inc-1765432199" to customer tickets for tracking.

deploy-bot: Status page update #2 published by maria (oncall) at 11:28 UTC.

jen (sre): mitigation holding. error rate steady ~3.2%. planning to drain 2 old hosts and ramp new ones with adjusted kernel flags. will update when resolved.

maria (oncall): if metrics hold for 20m, we'll prepare resolved notice. ops, please prepare resolved text and a short postmortem action item list.

ops (eng-ops): resolved notice draft: ```Resolved: The elevated error rate for /v1/generate in US-West has been resolved. Root cause: KV cache pressure causing intermittent worker OOMs after a model rollout; mitigations included rolling restarts, routing to fallback model variant, and scaling adjusted hosts. If you continue to experience issues, contact support.```

anna (marketing): suggest replacing technical root cause phrasing in public notice with: "increased caching pressure related to a recent model update" — keeps it readable for customers.

joe (legal): fine with that edit.

maria (oncall): publishing resolved notice in 30m if error rate <1% for the window. thanks all. :thumbsup:
